title: Professional Services Projects Rescheduling and Work Holds
content:
These are the Professional Services Projects rules for moving a scheduled start, pausing work and resuming it.

## Before kickoff: moving the scheduled start

Before kickoff the client may move the scheduled start. A move requested at least the class's reschedule notice in business days before the current scheduled start date is free, and a later one is charged the class reschedule fee.

| Notice given before the current scheduled start | Reschedule fee |
|---|---|
| the class notice in business days or more | none |
| fewer business days than the class notice | the class reschedule fee |

Hypothetical illustration: with a notice of 10 business days, a move requested 10 business days before the current scheduled start is free; one requested 9 business days before it is charged.

## After kickoff: holds

After kickoff, work is put on hold at the client's request, for an unmet client dependency, or when an invoice of the client is more than the class work stoppage threshold in days past due.

The former clause under which a client-caused hold (at the client's request, for an unmet client dependency or for non-payment) longer than the class hold limit let Stratton Bay terminate the engagement as a client cancellation or re-price the remaining work by change order is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current basis for long client-caused holds.

## On resumption

On resumption, the target completion date moves by the calendar days on hold.

The former clause under which, when a client-caused hold lasted more than the class remobilization threshold in calendar days, a remobilization fee of the class remobilization fee was invoiced is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current basis for remobilization fees.

Hypothetical illustration: an engagement on hold for 21 calendar days that resumes has its target completion date moved 21 calendar days later.
